description: single pole IIR alpha = 0.2 on complex samples vs single_pole_iir_filter_cc

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 4.999885560254813e-5 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 4.99969484284406: <= 3.429138609135315 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 4.999885560254813e-5 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (1.0 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 4.99969484284406: <= 5.928986030557345 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q17 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 1.2500095367727145e-5 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q17, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 5.000076295109477: <= 0.8723392712690589 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: GNU Radio keeps the state in double, this is f32: each step rounds the sum (terms of total size 0.5549999999999999) by 4 * 2^-24 at most, amplified by ||1/A(z)||_1 = 5.000000000000001: 0.0217 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.
